newsitem.title: USA: ABC vows to appeal Food Lion punitive damage award.
newsitem.headline: ABC vows to appeal Food Lion punitive damage award.

text.p: Walt Disney Co's ABC Television on Wednesday said it would appeal a jury award ordering the network to pay punitive damages of $5.5 million to Food Lion Inc.
ABC also defended the undercover techniques used in obtaining a story about the supermarket chain. The broadcast earlier led to a fraud verdict against the network.
In a statement, ABC News President Roone Arledge said ABC would appeal the verdict on punitive damages, issued on Wednesday morning.
"The verdict of the North Carolina jury should trouble every American -- especially every journalist," Arledge said.

Lawyers for Food Lion were successful in convincing the jury to "punish" ABC for using undercover investigative techniques, he said. Food Lion never challenged the truthfulness of the 1992 broadcast by "PrimeTime Live," but sued ABC for fraud.
Arledge said undercover techniques used by American journalists had proven effective for more than a century in exposing wrongdoing and prompting needed reforms.

"After finding that the use of those undercover techniques caused Food Lion only token damages, the jury has now awarded Food Lion punitive damages of 4,000 times that amount. That result in unconscionable," Arledge said in the statement.
Arledge said the jury's earlier award of compensatory damages of $1,400 sent ABC the message that news organizations would have to find another way to uncover the news.
ABC lead attorney Bill Jeffress said that ABC would file motion in federal court by February 21 to appeal the punitive damage award.
Food Lion is a unit of Belgian retailer Ets Delhaize Freres et Cie "LE LION" SA.
